Wait. (19,36) is… let me check: after reset, C is at 35-38. (19,36) is inside C's body. But G is empty after the click. Previously (T41) clicking (19,36) did select C. What changed?
Hmm, wait — actually, let me look at the image again. The image shows: g-ring at 11, G-ring at 23 (B is selected). Blobs are at 17, 23, 35.
Hold on — could it be that the blob at 35 is no longer C?! After the reset, are the blob identities the same? The reset restores positions, but the "identity" (target) is tied to the blob object. All three blobs are green and look identical. The blob at 35 should be C (target 23).
But wait — what if the reset re-randomized or reassigned the targets? Let me verify: click the blob at 35 and see where the g-ring appears. Clicking (19,36) gave G empty — that's weird in itself. Unless the click at (19,36) was interpreted as a click on… an empty cell? Is (19,36) empty? C's body: N columns are 35-38, rows 18-21. Let me check the exact cells of the blob at 35: from the previous scan, C@35's cells: (18,36),(18,37),(19,35),(19,36),(19,37),(19,38),(20,35),(20,36),(20,37),(20,38),(21,36),(21,37). So (19,36) is N.
So clicking (19,36) on C's body → G empty (deselected!). Then clicking (19,22) → B selected.
Hmm, wait, maybe the rule is: clicking a blob while another blob is selected deselects (toggles off)? Before this test, B was selected (from the LEFT test). Clicking C's body → G empty = deselected (not switched to C)! Then clicking (19,22) (empty cell near B) → B reselected??
But at T41: initial state (nothing selected), click (19,36) → C selected. Then click (19,30) (empty slot 29) → A selected. So from a deselected state, clicking an empty slot cell selected A?! (19,30) is slot 29 — empty. And A got selected. So clicking an empty slot cell selects the blob whose target is that slot?? (19,30) = slot 29 = A's target → A selected!
New model: clicking a slot cell (whether empty or occupied) selects the blob whose target is that slot!
- (19,30) = slot 29 = A's target → A selected ✓ (T41).
- (19,22) = slot 23 = C's target → C should be selected… but B got selected! ✗.
Hmm, no. (19,22) is the left-edge cell of slot 23. B is at 23. B got selected. So clicking an occupied slot selects the occupant. And (19,30) is an empty slot 29 → A (target 29) selected.
So the rule: clicking a slot cell: if occupied → select the occupant; if empty → select the blob whose target is that slot (i.e., the blob that would jump there)!
Verify with T48: nothing selected, click (19,22) (slot 23, B occupies) → B selected ✓.
Verify with this test: B selected, click (19,36) — C's body = slot 35, C occupies → C should be selected. But G is empty! ✗.
Hmm. Unless clicking the currently… no, B was selected, C is a different blob.
Wait, wait. Let me re-verify: was B really selected before this test? After the LEFT test: G was 22-27 (B selected) ✓. Then this test: click (19,36) → G empty.
So clicking C's body while B is selected → deselected. But at T41, clicking C's body while nothing was selected → C selected. And clicking A's body… at T36: B selected, click (19,18) (A's body) → A selected (switch). So switching via body-click worked at T36!
T36: B selected → click A's body → A selected. This time: B selected → click C's body → deselected. The difference??
Hmm, T36 was before the first reset. This time is after two resets. Did the reset change the behavior? Or… maybe the blob at 35 after the reset is not C, and clicking it… no, clicking any blob's body should select it.
Let me test directly: click (19,37) (C's body) again and check G. And click (19,18) (A's body) and check G. Also click (19,36) once more.
Actually, the pattern might be: clicking a blob's body toggles that blob's selection (select if unselected, deselect if selected). T36: B selected, click A (unselected) → A selected ✓. This time: B selected, click C (unselected) → C should be selected. But G is empty. ✗.
